makaleler.baslik: Negative pressure wound therapy for the prevention of surgical site complications in emergency laparotomies: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Acil Laparotomilerde Cerrahi Alan Komplikasyonları İçin NPWT
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Acil laparotomi geçiren 5371 hastayı içeren 23 çalışmalık meta-analizde, yara kapama için uygulanan NPWT standart pansumana kıyasla cerrahi alan enfeksiyonu riskini anlamlı düzeyde azalttı (risk oranı 0,53; %95 CI 0,41-0,68; I²=%68).
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Surgical site infections (SSIs) are common after emergency laparotomy and are associated with substantial morbidity, prolonged recovery, and increased health care costs. Negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has been increasingly used prophylactically on closed incisions in high-risk surgical patients; however, evidence supporting its effectiveness after emergency laparotomy remains heterogeneous. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to reassess the effectiveness of NPWT compared with standard postoperative dressings for the prevention of SSI and other wound-related complications following emergency laparotomy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook and PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for studies published from April 2, 2022, to December 10, 2025, updating a prior review. Randomized clinical trials and comparative observational studies evaluating NPWT versus standard dressings in adult patients undergoing emergency laparotomy were included. The primary outcome was SSI. Secondary outcomes included superficial and deep SSI, wound dehiscence, seroma, hematoma, and length of hospital stay. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE.
RESULTS: Twenty-three studies involving 5371 patients were included, of whom 2528 received NPWT. NPWT was associated with a significantly lower risk of SSI compared with standard dressings (risk ratio, 0.53; 95% CI 0.41-0.68), with moderate to substantial heterogeneity (I² = 68%). NPWT was also associated with reductions in superficial and deep SSI, seroma formation, and wound dehiscence, but not with organ/space SSI, hematoma, or length of hospital stay. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent direction of effect. Funnel plot asymmetry and a significant Egger test suggested small-study effects.
CONCLUSION: Among patients undergoing emergency laparotomy, prophylactic NPWT applied to closed incisions was associated with a lower risk of SSI and several wound-related complications compared with standard postoperative dressings. However, the certainty of evidence remains very low due to heterogeneity, risk of bias, and small-study effects, highlighting the need for large pragmatic multicenter randomized trials to better define the magnitude of benefit and optimal patient selection.
makaleler.dergi_tam: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES

makaleler.baslik: Surgical Versus Conservative Management for Adhesive Small Bowel Obstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Adheziv İnce Bağırsak Tıkanıklığında Cerrahi ve Konservatif Tedavi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 205.717 hastayı içeren 45 çalışmalık meta-analizde, cerrahi tedavi konservatif tedaviye göre daha düşük 5 yıllık nüks riski ile ilişkili bulunurken (OR 0,41; p<0,001), daha yüksek in-hospital mortalite (OR 1,87; p=0,010) ve komplikasyon oranları gösterdi.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the clinical outcomes of surgical versus conservative management for adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO) in adult and pediatric patients by evaluating clinical outcomes, including in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), in-hospital complications, 5-year recurrence, and 5-year reoperation.
METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Embase databases were searched for all randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies until March 2, 2026. Both adult and pediatric studies were included. Risk of bias (ROB) was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias 2 (RoB2) tool for RCTs, and the ROBINS-I tool for observational studies. A pairwise meta-analysis used a random-effects model to estimate the clinical outcomes. The odds ratio (OR) and mean difference (MD) were employed to analyze dichotomous and continuous outcomes, respectively, with heterogeneity assessed by the I2 statistic.
RESULTS: 45 studies were included (9 prospective studies, 33 retrospective studies, and 3 RCTs), with a total of 205,717 patients with ASBO. Forty studies involved adults, and five involved pediatric patients. The surgical management may be associated with higher in-hospital mortality (OR = 1.87; 95% CI 1.21-2.89; I2 = 63.68%, p = 0.010, very low certainty), more in-hospital complications (OR = 5.33; 95% CI 3.17-8.97; I2 = 76.89%, p < 0.001, very low certainty), and longer LOS (MD = 4.10; 95% CI 3.44-4.76; I2 = 98.81%, p < 0.001, very low certainty) compared with the conservative management. However, surgical management may be associated with a lower risk of 5-year recurrence (OR = 0.41; 95% CI 0.30-0.56; I2 = 78.44%, p < 0.001, low certainty) compared with conservative management. No statistically significant association was observed in 5-year reoperation between the surgical and conservative management (OR = 0.73; 95% CI 0.22-2.49; I2 = 21.28%, p = 0.620, very low certainty).
CONCLUSIONS: Surgical management may be associated with a lower risk of 5-year recurrence in patients with ASBO but may be associated with higher in-hospital mortality, more in-hospital complications, and a longer length of stay. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of substantial heterogeneity and risk of bias.

makaleler.baslik: Recommendations for the Multimodal Management of Malignant Bowel Obstructions: Results of a North American Multidisciplinary Delphi Consensus.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Malign Bağırsak Tıkanıklıklarının Multidisipliner Yönetimi İçin Öneriler
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Kuzey Amerikalı uzmanlar, malign bağırsak tıkanıklığı için %80 ve üzeri uzlaşı eşiğiyle 49 kanıta dayalı Delphi konsensüs önerisi oluşturdu. Bu bildirgeler; preoperatif değerlendirme, tıbbi, cerrahi ve palyatif yönetimi kapsamaktadır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is a challenging clinical problem requiring teams to balance complex oncologic disease, limited treatment options, and patient prognosis and values as they approach end of life. Presently, there is limited high-quality evidence to guide decision-making for MBO patients.
OBJECTIVE: A multidisciplinary modified Delphi process was undertaken to create guidance and support clinical decision-making in the medical and surgical care of this patient population.
METHODS: Multidisciplinary experts from all specialties regularly caring for MBO in Canada and the United States were invited for participation, including Acute Care Surgery, Surgical Oncology, Gynecologic Oncology, Gastroenterology, Radiology, Medical Oncology, and Palliative Care. Statements were evaluated through two rounds of surveys and a consensus meeting, with an a priori threshold of 80% agreement for approval.
RESULTS: Forty-nine final evidence-informed statements were included following expert consensus review pertaining to Patient Assessment, Medical Management, Surgical Management, and Palliative Management, in addition to a unifying definition of MBO. Consensus statements address aspects of complex MBO care, including but not limited to, optimal preoperative evaluation and multidisciplinary review; timing and use of steroids, motility, and antisecretory agents; contraindications to surgery; key facets of consent and perioperative decision making; framework for the nuanced use of gastrostomies and IV fluids in the end-of-life setting.
CONCLUSIONS: This Modified Delphi consensus provides multidisciplinary evidence-based recommendations for the care of patients with this challenging problem. These expert approved statements provide much-needed clinical guidance to support best care balanced with patient values and avoidance of undue harm.

makaleler.baslik: The relevance of leukocytosis in patients with severe trauma: a systematic review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Şiddetli Travma Hastalarında Lökositozun Önemi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 15.658 hastayı içeren sistemik derlemede, travma sonrası lökosit sayılarının referans değerlere kıyasla sürekli yüksek olduğu ve ortalama lökosit sayısının 10,26 x 10^9/L olduğu, ancak morbidite/mortalite ile güçlü kanıt ilişkisi bulunmadığı gösterildi.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Polytrauma remains a leading cause of death in individuals younger than 40 years and poses major challenges during early resuscitation and subsequent clinical management. Beyond early mortality from hemorrhage, post-traumatic inflammatory and infectious complications such as systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) are of increasing clinical relevance. Leukocyte count is a simple and routinely available laboratory parameter. This systematic review aimed to evaluate whether leukocyte count on admission is associated with post-traumatic complications and mortality.
METHODS: A systematic review in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines was conducted. PubMed/MEDLINE and EMBASE were systematically searched for original English-language clinical studies published between January 1, 2000, and July 31, 2025, that investigated leukocyte counts following adult polytrauma. After deduplication, 2,169 records were independently screened by three investigators based on titles and abstracts. Thirty-two reports were sought for retrieval, and 12 studies were finally included. Disagreements were resolved by consensus. Data on study characteristics, patient and injury characteristics, leukocyte counts and kinetics, and clinical outcomes were extracted and qualitatively synthesized. Study quality and risk of bias were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. A sample-size-weighted mean admission leukocyte count was calculated from the reported study-level means, and associations were analyzed using Spearman's rank correlation.
RESULTS: After subsequent screening 12 studies with overall 15,658 patients were finally included in the current review. Across all studies, leukocyte counts after trauma were elevated compared with reference values. The weighted mean leukocyte count across studies was 10.26 × 10^9/L. The proportion of blunt trauma was positively correlated with mean leukocyte count (rho = 0.775, p = 0.04). Pneumonia and SIRS were reported in three and four studies, respectively. One study reported higher mortality in patients with persistent leukocytosis after trauma.
CONCLUSIONS: This review demonstrates that leukocyte counts are consistently elevated following trauma. Although some studies suggested associations with morbidity and mortality, the available evidence remains insufficient for firm prognostic conclusions because of substantial heterogeneity and the predominantly retrospective design of the included studies. Further research should focus on leukocyte subpopulations, particularly neutrophils, to improve understanding of post-traumatic immune responses and their clinical relevance.

makaleler.baslik: Targeting indocyanine green where it matters most: a CRP-stratified cohort study in acute cholecystitis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Akut Kolesistitte İndosiyanin Yeşili ve CRP Stratifikasyonu
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Akut kolesistit nedeniyle acil kolesistektomi yapılan 221 hastada I/R kullanımının etkileri incelendi. Açığa geçiş yalnızca konvansiyonel kolda yaşandı (%8,8), en yüksek CRP tertilinde mutlak risk azalması %15,4 (NNT 6,5) olarak hesaplandı.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence cholangiography has been linked to fewer conversions to open surgery in emergency cholecystectomy, but it adds cost, and evidence for its effect on conversion and operative time is graded moderate to low even by the consensus statement recommending routine use. We asked whether preoperative C-reactive protein (CRP), a marker of surgical difficulty and conversion risk, identifies patients in whom ICG's benefit is greatest.
METHODS: Prospective cohort of 221 patients undergoing emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis, stratified by ICG use (85 ICG vs 136 conventional). We tested the interaction between CRP and ICG use on conversion using Firth penalized logistic regression, and on operative time, length of stay, and complications using linear/logistic regression with a log-CRP sensitivity analysis. We compared conversion rates across CRP tertiles and calculated a CRP-stratified estimated absolute risk reduction (ARR) and number needed to treat (NNT).
RESULTS: Conversion occurred only in the conventional arm (12/136, 8.8%; 0/85 ICG), rising from 0 to 15.4% across CRP tertiles. The formal CRP×ICG interaction for conversion was not significant (Firth model, p = 0.878), reflecting the absence of ICG-arm events; the ARR associated with ICG use rose from not estimable to 9.8 points (95% CI 3.9-22.5; NNT≈10) in the middle tertile and 15.4 points (95% CI 8.0-27.5; NNT 6.5) in the highest. The interaction was significant for operative time (p = 0.045), strengthening under a log-CRP sensitivity model (p = 0.001), with CRP-related lengthening of surgery markedly smaller in the ICG arm.
CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, ICG's clinical benefit was not uniform across the CRP range. The CRP×ICG interaction reached significance for operative time; for conversion, the pattern was consistent and clinically plausible but not statistically significant, and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. A CRP-informed strategy for prioritising ICG may be worth testing prospectively.

turk.baslik: Evaluation of predictive factors for morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing surgery for peptic ulcer perforation.
turk.baslik_tr: Peptik Üser Perforasyonunda Morbidite ve Mortalite Belirteçleri
turk.kisa_ozet: Peptik ülser perforasyonu nedeniyle ameliyat edilen 319 hastanın incelendiği retrospektif çalışmada, MII-2 indeksi ve CRP/lenfosit oranı mortaliteyi öngörmede yüksek doğruluk gösterdi (AUC: 0,780 ve 0,787, p<0,001).
turk.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Peptic ulcer perforation (PUP) is a life-threatening complication with high mortality caused by the leakage of gastric contents into the peritoneal cavity, leading to peritonitis. Systemic inflammatory indices, such as the C-reactive protein (CRP)/lymphocyte ratio, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and multi-inflammatory indices (MII), reflect inflammation severity. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of the CRP/Lymphocyte ratio, NLR, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and MII indices for estimating morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing surgery for PUP.
METHODS: This retrospective analysis included 319 patients who underwent surgery for PUP between October 2012 and January 2025. Pre-operative inflammatory indices were calculated from laboratory data and correlated with post-operative complications, length of hospital stay, and mortality.
RESULTS: Higher CRP/Lymphocyte ratio, PLR, MII-1, MII-2, and MII-3 values were associated with fatal outcomes (p<0.05). The MII-2 and MII-3 indices best predicted post-operative complications with superior area under the curve (AUC) values (AUC: 0.655, 0.661, respectively) (p<0.001). All analyzed markers were significantly elevated in patients with prolonged hospitalization. Notably, the MII-2 index and CRP/lymphocyte ratio showed balanced sensitivity and high specificity for predicting mortality (AUC: 0.780, 0.787, respectively) (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: The MII-2 index and CRP-to-lymphocyte ratio are strong predictors of mortality in PUP patients, whereas the MII-2 and MII-3 indices are most effective for predicting complications. Incorporating these easily calculated indices into clinical practice can enhance risk stratification and decision-making.

tez.baslik: Deneysel superior mezenterik arter iskemi/reperfüzyon modelinde salisilaldehitten üretilen 1,2,3 triazol bileşeninin apoptozis üzerine etkisi
tez.baslik_tr: Deneysel İntestinal İskemi Reperfüzyon Hasarında Triazol Etkisi
tez.kisa_ozet: 24 sıçan üzerinde yapılan deneysel modelde, salisilaldehitten üretilen triazol bileşeninin intestinal iskemi/reperfüzyon hasarında TAS değerini artırdığı, OSI ve IL-6 düzeylerini azalttığı ve antiapoptotik etki sağladığı gösterildi (p<0,001).
tez.ozet: Amaç: İntestinal I/R hasarı, mezenterik kan akımında azalma/kesilme sonucu iskemi ve sonrasındaki reperfüzyona bağlı gelişen aşırı inflamatuvar ve oksidatif yanıt ile karakterize kompleks patofizyolojik bir durumdur. Yüksek morbidite ve mortalite ile seyreden ciddi klinik bir durum olmasına rağmen etkin bir tedavisi bulunmamaktadır. Bu çalışmadaki temel hipotez I/R'daki ksantin oksidaz inhibisyonu veya ekspresyonunun baskılanması ile apoptozisin azaltılabilmesidir. Çalışmanın primer amacı ksantin oksidaz inhibitörü olarak Salisilaldehitten üretilen 1, 2, 3 Triazol bileşeninin (SP123T) I/R hasarında apoptozis üzerine etkisinin ortaya konulmasıdır. Gereç ve Yöntem: Bu çalışma, 20-24 haftalık toplam 24 adet Spraque cinsi erkek sıçan üzerinde yapıldı. Sıçanlar her grupta 8 adet sıçan olacak şekilde 3 eşit gruba ayrıldı. Grup S (Sham) (n=8): Laparatomi, Grup C (Kontrol) (n=8): Laparatomi + İskemi reperfüzyon, Grup T (Triazol) (n=8): intraperitoneal 20 mg/kg triazol + Laparatomi + İskemi reperfüzyon. İskemi modelinde Superior mezenterik arter klemplenerek 1 saat iskemi ve 2 saat reperfüzyon uygulandı. Biyokimyasal olarak kan örneklerinde TAS, TOS, OSI, Ksantin oksidaz, IL-6 ve IL-10 çalışıldı. Karaciğer ve terminal ileumda doku örneklerinde ksantin oksidaz, ürik asit çalışıldı. Karaciğet ve terminal ileum doku örneklerinde histopatoloji skorları ve Bax, Bcl-2 apoptozİs markerları çalışıldı. Bulgular: Bu çalışmada Salisilaldehitten üretilen 1, 2, 3 Triazol uygulamasının TAS değerini arttırdığı ve OSI'ini azalttığı tespit edildi (p=0.05, p<0.001). IL-6 ve IL-10 düzeylerini anlamlı düzeyde azalltığı görüldü (p<0.001, p=0.003). Karaciğer/barsak ksantin oksidaz düzeylerini azaltarak kan ve karaciğer ürik asit düzeylerini anlamlı düzeyde azalttığı tespit edildi (p<0.001, p: 0.010, p<0.001). IHS, LHS-Vac ve LHS-Nec oranlarını anlamlı düzeyde azaltarak histopatolojik hasarın azaldığı tespit edildi (p= 0.009, p=0.020, p=0.012). İntestinal ve karaciğer Bcl-2 düzeylerinde artış ve karaciğer Bax/Bcl-2 oranını arttırarak (p=0.033, P<0.001, p=0.022) antiapoptotik etki potansiyeline sahip olduğu görüldü. Sonuç: Bu çalışmada SP123T bileşeninin intestinal I/R hasarında terminal ileum ve karaciğer üzerinde protektif etkisi olduğu ortaya konuldu. Protektif etki mekanizmasının ksantin oksidaz ekspresyonunda azalma ile oksidatif stresin azaltılması ve antiapoptotik bcl-2 ekspresyonunda artış mekanizması ile de antiapoptotik etkiye bağlı olduğu tespit edildi. Bu çalışma sonuçları SP123T bileşeninin intestinal I/R hasarında protektif bir ajan olarak kullanılabileceğini etki mekanizmaları ile birlikte ortaya koyan ilk deneysel çalışmadır. Bu çalışma sonuçlarının farklı dozlarda ve daha fazla sayıda örneklem büyüklüğünde yapılacak deneysel çalışmalar ile desteklenmesi gerekmektedir. Elde edilecek yeni sonuçlar ile birlikte SP123T bileşeninin intestinal I/R hasarını önlemede klinik pratikte kullanılabilecek translasyonel protektif bir molekül olabileceği öngörülmektedir. Klinik pratikte kullanılabilmesi durumunda yüksek mortalite riskine sahip akut mezenterik iskemi, travmatik şok, laparoskopik cerrahi ve majör abdominal cerrahilerde I/R hasarını önlemede potansiyel bir teröpatik ajan olabilir. Anahtar kelimeler: Triazol, iskemi, reperfüzyon, apoptozis, Bax, Bcl-2, SP123T, ksantin oksidaz

makaleler.baslik: Acetic acid chromoendoscopy for detection of neoplastic Barrett's oesophagus: stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial (ACID-trial).
makaleler.baslik_tr: Barrett Özofagus Sürveyansında Asetik Asit Kromoendoskopi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 2267 hastanın dahil olduğu çok merkezli step-wedge RCT'de, asetik asit kromoendoskopinin neoplazi saptama oranını artırmadığı gösterildi (%7,4'e karşı %7,1; OR 0,97; %95 CI 0,65-1,44).
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies.
DESIGN: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial.
SETTING: 18 Dutch community hospitals.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia.
INTERVENTIONS: Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies.
RESULTS: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24).
CONCLUSIONS: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl; NL-OMON25059 (prospective registration; 4 Dec 2019).

makaleler.baslik: Cold versus hot snare endoscopic mucosal resection for 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps: a multicenter randomized trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: 10-19 mm Kolorektal Poliplerde Soğuk ve Sıcak Snare EMR
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 233 polibin alındığı çok merkezli RCT'de, soğuk snare EMR tam histolojik rezeksiyon açısından sıcak snare EMR'ye benzer bulundu (%90,4'e karşı %93,2; fark -%2,7; %95 CI -%9,8 - %4,3). Soğuk grupta işlem içi kanama daha sık görüldü (%19,1'e karşı %3,4).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Evidence for cold snare endoscopic mucosal resection (CS-EMR) in 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps is scarce. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) to compare CS-EMR against hot snare EMR (HS-EMR) in this setting.
METHODS: We enrolled patients with 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps from 15 centers. Eligible polyps were individually randomized (1:1) to CS-EMR or HS-EMR. The primary outcome was histologic complete resection, analyzed in modified intention-to-treat (mITT) and per-protocol (PP) populations (noninferiority margin -10%). Secondary outcomes included en bloc resection, intraprocedural and delayed adverse events, and resection time.
RESULTS: 216 patients with 233 eligible polyps were included (CS-EMR 116; HS-EMR 117). In the mITT analysis, complete resection was 90.4% in the CS-EMR group and 93.2% in the HS-EMR group (difference -2.7%, 95%CI -9.8 to 4.3), showing noninferiority of CS-EMR vs. HS-EMR. PP results were consistent (CS-EMR 93.3%; HS-EMR 93.2%; difference 0.2%, 95%CI -6.7 to 7.1). CS-EMR was noninferior for 10-14-mm polyps (94.3% vs. 94.0%; 95%CI -6.8 to 7.2) but not for 15-19-mm polyps (78.6% vs. 90.9%; 95%CI -30.4 to 5.8), although interaction was not significant. En bloc resection rates and resection time were similar between groups. Intraprocedural bleeding was more frequent with CS-EMR (19.1% vs. 3.4%), whereas delayed bleeding was rare (0.0% vs. 0.9%), and no perforation occurred in either group.
CONCLUSION: CS-EMR was noninferior to HS-EMR for histologic complete resection of 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps, but its applicability to 15-19-mm lesions remains uncertain.

makaleler.baslik: Meta-analysis of single session versus two-stage endoscopic ultrasound directed transgastric ERCP (EDGE) in gastric bypass patients.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Gastrik Bypass Hastalarında Tek ve İki Seanslı EDGE Meta-Analizi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 7 gözlemsel çalışmanın dahil olduğu 346 hastalığı içeren meta-analizde, tek seanslı ve iki seanslı EDGE yöntemleri arasında teknik başarı, klinik başarı ve komplikasyonlar açısından anlamlı fark saptanmadı (OR 1,45; %95 CI 0,38-5,48; p=0,58).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Studies have shown variable outcomes when comparing single session endoscopic ultrasound directed transgastric endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (SS EDGE) and two-stage EDGE. We conducted a meta-analysis.
METHODS: Online databases were searched for studies comparing SS EDGE to two-stage EDGE in patients with gastric bypass. The outcomes of interest were technical success, clinical success, stent dislodgement/migration, overall adverse events (AEs), persistent fistula and patients with weight gain. Pooled odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated.
RESULTS: A total of 7 observational studies with 346 patients (47% SS EDGE, 53% two-stage EDGE) were included. The mean age was 58 years and 23% patients were males. Around 80% EDGE procedures were done for biliary pathologies with the rest being for pancreatic pathologies. When comparing the two approaches, no significant differences were found with respect to technical success (OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.03 to 3.53, p = 0.37), clinical success (OR 1.88, 95% CI 0.38 to 9.17, p = 0.44), stent dislodgement/migration (OR 1.70, 95% CI 0.88 to 3.31, p = 0.12), overall AEs (OR 1.45, 95% CI 0.38 to 5.48, p = 0.58), persistent fistula (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.32 to 3.09, p = 0.99), and patients with weight gain (OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.32 to 4.84, p = 0.75).
CONCLUSION: SS EDGE and two-stage EDGE were found to have similar outcomes in terms of efficacy and safety.

makaleler.baslik: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) for endoscopic resection of upper gastrointestinal lesions ≤ 2 cm: a single-center, 1:2 randomized, controlled, non-inferiority trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Üst Gİ Lezyonlarında Endoskopik Rezeksiyon için ERAS
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 165 hastanın dahil olduğu tek merkezli RCT'de, ERAS protokolü postoperatif komplikasyonlar açısından geleneksel yönteme göre non-inferior bulundu (risk farkı -%0,91; %90 CI -%3,97 - %3,83). ERAS grubu daha kısa hastanede kalış süresi ve daha düşük maliyet gösterdi.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to preliminarily evaluate the non-inferiority of ERAS-based perioperative management in endoscopic resection for upper gastrointestinal lesions.
METHODS: A total of 165 patients with upper gastrointestinal lesions ≤ 2 cm undergoing endoscopic resection (STER, ESD, ESE, or EFTR) were randomized 1:2 to the ERAS group (n = 55) or the conventional recovery after surgery (CRAS) group (n = 110). The primary outcome was postoperative complication rate, with a non-inferiority margin of 5%. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, recovery indicators, length of stay, and hospitalization costs.
RESULTS: The risk difference in postoperative complications between the ERAS group and the CRAS group was - 0.91% (90% CI [- 3.97% to 3.83%]), meeting the prespecified criterion for non-inferiority. The ERAS group also showed significantly lower VAS pain scores (0.0 [0.0-3.0] vs. 2.0 [0.0-3.3]; p = 0.020), shorter nasogastric tube duration (3.0 [2.0-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-4.0] days; p < 0.001), and earlier time to first oral water (23.9 [18.5-32.5] vs. 64.7 [56.2-77.0] hours; p < 0.001), first oral feeding (33.2 [22.5-38.5] vs. 70.3 [59.2-79.8] hours; p < 0.001), and first ambulation (36.8 [27.0-45.5] vs. 76.1 [62.0-86.0] hours; p < 0.001). Postoperative length of stay, total length of stay, and hospitalization costs were also significantly reduced (all p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this single-center trial involving selected patients with upper gastrointestinal lesions ≤ 2 cm, ERAS met the prespecified criterion for non-inferiority to CRAS with respect to postoperative complications. ERAS was also associated with shorter hospital stays and lower hospitalization costs.

makaleler.baslik: Endoscopic ultrasound in hepatology: A European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Technical and Technology Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Hepatolojide Endoskopik Ultrasonografi: ESGE İncelemesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Avrupa Gastrointestinal Endoskopi Derneği teknik incelemesinde, karaciğer hastalıkları ve portal hipertansiyonda EUS kılavuzluğundaki tekniklerin güncel kanıtları değerlendirilerek GRADE çerçevesine göre öneriler geliştirilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided techniques are increasingly applied in hepatology, including for tissue acquisition, vascular access, pressure measurement, and selected therapeutic interventions. However, adoption remains heterogeneous because of variability in technical approaches, devices, outcome definitions, operator expertise, and the quality of available evidence.
METHODS: This European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Technical and Technology Review summarizes the current evidence on selected EUS-guided techniques in liver disease and portal hypertension, including liver stiffness assessment, focal liver lesion characterization and sampling, EUS-guided liver biopsy, EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement, therapy for gastric varices, and portal vein sampling for liquid biopsy applications. Evidence was identified through a structured literature search up to April 2026, and recommendation statements were graded using the GRADE framework.
RESULTS: Eight ESGE statements were developed. The available evidence supports selected use of EUS-guided shear wave elastography and contrast-enhanced EUS as adjunctive techniques; EUS-guided liver biopsy and EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement as complementary approaches in selected patients and expert centers; and EUS-guided treatment of gastric varices as a valid alternative to direct endoscopic injection where appropriate expertise is available. Portal vein sampling remains investigational. Across the indications, the evidence base is limited by small studies, heterogeneous techniques, variable outcome definitions, and limited prospective comparative data.
CONCLUSIONS: This review provides an evidence-based framework for the selective use of EUS-guided techniques in hepatology and portal hypertension. Wider adoption will require standardized techniques, structured training, consistent outcome definitions, and prospective comparative studies.

turk.baslik: Pre-procedural predictors of in-hospital mortality in ICU patients undergoing endoscopic PEG placement.
turk.baslik_tr: Yoğun Bakımda PEG Uygulanan Hastalarda Mortalite Prediktörleri
turk.kisa_ozet: Yoğun bakımda PEG yapılan 364 hastanın retrospektif cohort çalışmasında, hastane içi mortalite %34,3 olarak saptandı. Aktif enfeksiyon (OR 3,62; p < 0,001), düşük albümin (OR 0,90; p < 0,001) ve yüksek üre düzeyleri bağımsız mortalite prediktörleri olarak belirlendi.
turk.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) is widely used to provide long-term enteral nutrition in patients unable to maintain oral intake. However, PEG placement is already considered a high-risk intervention in the intensive care unit (ICU), where short-term mortality is substantial. This study aimed to identify predictors of in-hospital mortality in ICU patients undergoing PEG.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary center from 2019 to 2024, including all consecutive adult ICU patients who underwent endoscopic PEG. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and procedural data were analyzed. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were used to identify independent predictors.
RESULTS: A total of 364 ICU patients underwent PEG, of whom 125 (34.3%) died during the index hospitalization. Among non-survivors, 56 (44.8%) died within the first 14 days after PEG placement. Non-survivors showed lower albumin levels (24.4 vs. 28.2 g/L; p<0.001), higher urea concentrations (57.1 vs. 40.6 mg/dL; p<0.001), higher neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (6.44 vs. 4.81; p=0.002), and more frequent infection at the time of PEG (88% vs. 58.6%; p<0.001). Prolonged mechanical ventilation (>14 days) was more common among non-survivors (23.2% vs. 11.7%; p=0.005). In the multivariate model, active infection [odds ratio (OR) 3.62; p<0.001], lower albumin (OR 0.90 per g/L; p<0.001), and higher urea (OR 1.02; p=0.05) independently predicted in-hospital mortality, whereas prolonged intubation showed a strong trend but did not reach significance (OR 1.85; p=0.06).
CONCLUSION: ICU patients with active infection, severe hypoalbuminemia, and elevated urea levels have a markedly increased risk of in-hospital mortality after PEG placement. Prolonged mechanical ventilation appears to characterize a clinically more fragile ICU population rather than serving as an independent predictor of mortality. Incorporating these objective markers into pre-procedural assessments may improve patient selection and support decision-making in the ICU.

tez.baslik: Laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahide piyes çıkarım yerinin insizyonel herni gelişimi üzerine etkisi: Retrospektif bir analiz
tez.baslik_tr: Laparoskopik Kolorektal Cerrahide İnsizyonel Herni Gelişimi ve Risk Faktörleri
tez.kisa_ozet: Laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahi geçiren 80 hastanın incelendiği retrospektif çalışmada insizyonel herni oranı %13,7 bulundu. Çok değişkenli analize göre ileri yaş (>60) bağımsız risk faktörü olarak saptandı (OR 0,184; p = 0,034), piyes çıkarım insizyon yerinin ise herni ile anlamlı ilişkisi görülmedi.
tez.ozet: Giriş ve Amaç: Laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahi, minimal invaziv yapısı ve onkolojik açıdan açık cerrahiye eşdeğer sonuçları nedeniyle günümüzde sık kullanılan bir prosedürdür. Bununla birlikte, piyes çıkarımı için ek insizyon gerekliliği, karın duvarında zayıf alan oluşturarak, insizyonel herni gelişimi için önemli bir risk faktörüdür. Literatürde farklı insizyon tiplerinin herni oranlarını etkileyebileceği bildirilmektedir. Bu çalışmanın amacı, hastanemizde laparoskopik kolon ve rektum cerrahisi yapılan olgularda piyes çıkarma insizyonunun lokalizasyonu ile insizyonel herni gelişimi arasındaki ilişkinin değerlendirilmesi ve aynı zamanda herni gelişiminde etkili olabilecek hasta ve cerrahi faktörlerin analiz edilmesidir. Gereç ve Yöntem: Bu retrospektif çalışma, SBÜ Gazi Yaşargil Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesinde 2023–2025 yılları arasında laparoskopik kolon veya rektum cerrahisi yapılan 18 yaş ve üzeri 96 hastanın dosya kayıtlarının retrospektif incelenmesiyle gerçekleştirildi Altı aydan daha kısa süre takibi bulunan olgular çalışmaya alınmadı. Koşulları karşılayan 80 hasta çalışmaya dahil edildi. Hastalara ait demografik veriler, komorbid hastalıklar, laboratuvar parametreleri, tümör özellikleri, cerrahi teknik detayları, piyes çıkarım insizyonu ve postoperatif komplikasyonlar değerlendirildi. İnsizyonel herni tanısı fizik muayene ve görüntüleme yöntemleriyle doğrulandı. Bulgular: İnsizyonel herni oranı çalışmamızda %13,7 olarak saptanmıştır. İH gelişen grupta yaş anlamlı olarak daha yüksek bulunmuştur (p=0,028). Lojistik regresyon analizi yoluyla insizyonel herni ile ilişkili faktörlerin çok değişkenli analizinin sonuçlarına göre (Tablo 13); yaş >60 (OR:0,184, 95% CI; 0,038-0,883, p: 0,034) olması bağımsız risk faktörü olarak ortaya konmuştur.Preoperatif CEA düzeyi herni gelişen hastalarda daha yüksekti. Cinsiyet, VKİ, diyabet, hipertansiyon, KOAH ve diğer komorbiditelerin herni gelişimi üzerinde anlamlı etkisi görülmedi. Ayrıca cerrahi prosedür tipi, tümör lokalizasyonu ve patoloji dağılımı açısından gruplar arasında anlamlı fark bulunmadı. Piyes çıkarma insizyonu ile insizyonel herni gelişimi arasında istatistiksel olarak anlamlı ilişki tespit edilmedi. Sonuç: Bu çalışma, laparoskopik kolorektal cerrahide insizyonel herni gelişiminde cerrahi teknikten ziyade hastaya özgü biyolojik faktörlerin daha belirleyici olduğunu göstermektedir. Özellikle ileri yaş ve yüksek CEA düzeyi herni gelişimi açısından dikkat edilmesi gereken parametrelerdir. Laparoskopik cerrahide kullanılan piyes çıkarım insizyonunun herni riskini belirlemede tek başına yeterli olmayabilir, hasta bazlı risk değerlendirmesiyle kombine edilmesi daha uygun olabilir.

makaleler.baslik: Simulation-Based Education in Competency-Based Health Professional Training: A Scoping Umbrella Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Sağlık Eğitiminde Simülasyona Dayalı Eğitimin İncelenmesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Bu şemsiye derleme, 44 inceleme üzerinden sağlık meslekleri eğitiminde simülasyona dayalı eğitimin bilgi, beceri ve klinik muhakemeyi desteklemede nasıl kullanıldığını incelemiştir. Çalışma, simülasyonun müfredata uzunlamasına entegre edilmesinde eksiklikler olduğunu ortaya koymuştur.
makaleler.ozet: Statement: Competency-based education (CBE) has become a prevalent framework in health professions education, emphasizing observable outcomes, learner progression, and accountability to patient needs. This scoping umbrella review examined how simulation-based education (SBE) is being used to support and implement CBE across health care professions and disciplines. Across 44 reviews, SBE was used to support knowledge, skills, clinical reasoning, communication, teamwork, and confidence. High-fidelity simulation, virtual reality, standardized patients, and hybrid modalities were commonly used to support deliberate practice and competency-focused learning. Despite this alignment, SBE was frequently implemented as a discrete educational modality rather than as a longitudinally integrated component of competency-based curricula, with inconsistent reporting of competency frameworks, theory-informed design, debriefing approaches, and programmatic assessment strategies. This review synthesizes key findings, gaps, and recommendations and proposes a simulation-grounded CBE framework to guide the intentional integration of SBE within competency-based health care curricula.

makaleler.baslik: Microsurgical Training and Skill Acquisition: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Mikrocerrahi Eğitimi ve Beceri Kazanımının Sistematik İncelemesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Bu sistematik derleme ve meta-analiz, mikrocerrahi beceri kazanımında uygun modelin hangisi olduğunu değerlendirmiştir. Tüm simülasyon modelleriyle yapılan eğitimin, mikrocerrahi becerilerde büyük ve istatistiksel olarak anlamlı gelişmeler sağladığı görülmüştür.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Simulation in the context of microsurgical training has been explored and examined in the literature with a difference of opinion regarding the optimal model to use for the training and acquisition of microsurgical skills. In some reports, the fidelity of the live animal models offers the opportunity learn surgical as well as surgical-scenario contextualized skills that a less realistic model is unable to offer. In other publications, the skills that can be taught on lower fidelity models are equivalent and offer a more viable and feasible approach to surgical training.
METHODS: A systematic review of the available microsurgical simulation models was performed with a focus on the acquisition of microsurgical skills measured with validated microsurgical instruments. A meta-analysis of the subgroups was then performed to identify the optimal microsurgical training tool.
RESULTS: All training with simulation models resulted in large and statistically significant improvements in microsurgical skills across the range of groupings of microsurgical simulations. This effect was consistently identified across the different groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Choosing a model to train microsurgical skills may be less important than initially thought. Across the range of living and nonliving biological models and synthetic models, the potential to improve microsurgical skills significantly is available regardless of which simulation model is chosen.
makaleler.dergi_tam: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open

makaleler.baslik: Optimizing video review for general surgery residents: a prospective observational study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Genel Cerrahi Asistanları için Video İncelemesinin Optimizasyonu
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Bu tek merkezli prospektif kohort çalışmasında 13 asistan değerlendirilmiştir. Uzman koç eşliğinde rehberli video incelemesi en faydalı yöntem olarak derecelendirilmiş (ortalama 4,9/5) olup, modaliteler arasındaki fark anlamlı bulunmuştur (ANOVA F(3,48)=6,53, p<0,001).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Surgical video review is increasingly used to support self-reflection and technical skill development. However, little is known about which aspects of video review are the most effective for general surgery residents. We hypothesize that senior residents would find self-review most helpful while junior residents would benefit more from guided review with an attending coach.
METHODS: In this single institution prospective cohort study, residents reviewed hepatocystic triangle dissection videos cropped from laparoscopic cholecystectomy operations captured on OR Black Box where the resident was the primary surgeon during this portion of the case. Over one-hour sessions, residents completed four structured video review modalities: standardized public video, peer video, self-review, and attending coach-guided review. Attending coaches were fellowship-trained MIS faculty with surgical education training. Outcomes included perceived usefulness (5-point Likert-type scale) and modified Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills (mOSAT) scores.
RESULTS: Thirteen residents (5 seniors, 38.5% completed PGY 3-year or more) participated, having completed a mean of 72.2 (SD 36.7) laparoscopic cholecystectomies. Attending coach-guided review was rated most helpful (mean = 4.9/5), followed by self-review (4.2/5), peer video (3.3/5), and standardized public video (2.9/5). Differences across modalities were significant (ANOVA F(3,48)=6.53, p < 0.001). Junior residents tended to overestimate their performance compared to blinded coach assessment significantly more than senior residents (- 4.4 vs 1.8, p = 0.038).
CONCLUSIONS: Attending coach-guided video review is perceived as most useful by residents at all levels. The time investment of attending coaches appears worthwhile, as both junior and senior residents benefit most from guided expert reflection. Incorporating structured video review sessions with attending coaches could enhance surgical residency training in technical skills, decision-making, and self-assessment.

makaleler.baslik: Extended Reality, Telementoring, and Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Assessment in Surgical Training: A Narrative Review.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Cerrahi Eğitimde XR, Telementoring ve Yapay Zekâ
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Bu derlemede 67 çalışma incelenmiş ve VR simülasyonunun teknik beceri kazanımında olgun bir araç olduğu, yapay zekâ destekli değerlendirmenin ise uzman derecelendirmeleriyle %65 ila %77 oranında uyum sağladığı gösterilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: The Halstedian apprenticeship model in surgical training faces escalating pressure from work-hour restrictions, rising operative complexity, and heightened patient-safety expectations. Extended reality (XR) technologies-virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR)-together with telementoring platforms and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment, are frequently proposed as responses to these pressures. This narrative review examines what the evidence currently supports, for whom, and with what methodological certainty.
DESIGN: A structured narrative review was performed and reported with reference to PRISMA 2020 principles for source flow and to the SANRA framework for narrative-review quality. Titles and abstracts were screened independently by 2 reviewers and disagreements resolved by consensus. Seminal pre-2014 sources were retained through hand-searching of reference lists for conceptual and historical context. Findings were synthesized narratively in 3 stages (independent reading, inductive coding, consensus theme definition); quantitative pooling was not performed.
SETTING: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for records published between January 1, 2014, and May 31, 2026, using the string: (("extended reality" OR "virtual reality" OR "augmented reality" OR "mixed reality" OR "XR" OR "VR" OR "AR" OR "head-mounted display") AND ("surgical education" OR "surgical training" OR "surgical simulation" OR "operative training" OR "laparoscopic training")) OR (("telementoring" OR "teleproctoring" OR "remote mentoring" OR "telesurgery") AND ("surgical" OR "surgery" OR "laparoscopic")) OR (("artificial intelligence" OR "machine learning" OR "deep learning" OR "computer vision") AND ("surgical assessment" OR "surgical simulation" OR "surgical skills" OR "operative performance")).
PARTICIPANTS: Not applicable at the patient level; the included sources involved medical students, surgical residents, and practicing surgeons across surgical specialties.
RESULTS: Of 8113 records identified, 252 full-text reports were assessed and 67 met eligibility criteria; 50 sources were prioritized for the synthesis: 40 empirical or secondary evidence sources (VR and immersive simulation including haptics, n = 12; AR and MR, n = 7; telementoring and telesurgery, n = 9; AI-assisted assessment and adaptive learning, n = 11; emerging technologies, n = 1) and 10 conceptual, methodological, or regulatory sources. Thirty-six sources fell within the search window and 14 were foundational pre-2014 sources. VR simulation is supported by the strongest evidence base, including randomized trials and pooled analyses showing reduced operative time and intraoperative error and demonstrable transfer to the operating room; participants are predominantly residents and medical students. AR evidence is concentrated in image-guided orthopedic and spinal navigation performed by practicing surgeons, with 1 randomized trial of AR telestration in laparoscopic training. Telementoring evidence relates predominantly to practicing surgeons and proctored credentialing rather than to residency-level graduate medical education. AI-assisted assessment achieves agreement with expert raters in the reported range of 65% to 77% across global skill domains but remains largely single-center and retrospective.
CONCLUSIONS: The evidence supports XR simulation as a mature adjunct for technical skill acquisition at the "Shows How" level of Miller's pyramid, whereas telementoring and AI-assisted assessment remain, in the main, technologies validated outside graduate surgical education. Evidence is strongest at Kirkpatrick Levels 1-2 and weakest at Level 4. The field's principal deficit is no longer proof of concept but implementation science and patient-level outcome validation.

makaleler.baslik: A Pocketbook to Enhance Intraoperative Learning on the Core Surgery Clerkship: A Mixed Methods Study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Cerrahi Stajında Ameliyathane Öğrenimini Geliştiren Cep Kitabı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 39 tıp öğrencisiyle yapılan karma yöntemli çalışmada, cep kitabı kullanımı sonrasında ameliyathane katılımının arttığı (p<0,05) ve öğrencilerin %95,2'sinin katıldığı belirtilmiştir.
makaleler.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether a Surgical Cases Pocketbook enhances medical student engagement and perceived learning in the operating room (OR) during the core surgery clerkship.
DESIGN: Explanatory sequential mixed-methods study. Quantitative surveys on Pocketbook use, perceived utility, engagement, and confidence were followed by inductive thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews.
SETTING: Core surgery clerkship at a single academic institution.
PARTICIPANTS: Third-year medical students (39 eligible students) on the core surgery clerkship between April and December 2025. Twenty-seven students completed the survey (69.2% participation rate); 11 of the surveyed students (40.7% of survey participants) completed interviews.
RESULTS: Most students adopted the Pocketbook (77.8% of survey respondents); the majority used it at least weekly (66.7%). Students rated the anatomical landmarks and surgical steps as most useful and the reflective/patient documentation sections as least useful. OR engagement increased after Pocketbook use (Wilcoxon signed-rank test median change +1 Likert point on 5-point scale, p < 0.05) with 95.2% of students classified as "Engaged" after use and no students becoming less engaged. Case preparation confidence was higher for Pocketbook-included cases (Wilcoxon signed-rank test median change +1 Likert point on 5-point scale, p < 0.05). Qualitative analysis demonstrated that the Pocketbook functioned as a concise, medical student-level framework that reduced cognitive load, oriented students intraoperatively, and helped transform passive observation into active participation. However, the Pocketbook's impact was mediated by OR power dynamics and psychological safety.
CONCLUSIONS: The Pocketbook appears to provide an effective framework for student-driven OR preparation and thus active intraoperative learning. The Pocketbook was widely adopted and associated with increased self-reported OR engagement and case preparation confidence; these engagement and confidence gains were contextualized by the interpersonal climate of the OR. Future study may reveal ideal Pocketbook incorporation into clerkship experiences to optimize student intraoperative learning and engagement.

makaleler.baslik: Palliative Care in Surgery: Updated Research Priorities from the Surgical Palliative Care Research Expert Consensus Conference.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Cerrahi Palyatif Bakım: Güncellenmiş Araştırma Öncelikleri
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 28 uzmanın katıldığı konsensus konferansında, cerrahi palyatif bakım için hasta seçimi, müdahaleler ve sonuç ölçümü alanlarında 11 araştırma boşluğu belirlendi. Gelişmiş veri sistemlerinin hasta tanımlama süreçlerini destekleyebileceği vurgulandı.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Surgical palliative care (SPC) research has advanced since the 2017 research agenda, but persistent gaps in patient selection, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement limit implementation across evolving surgical care settings.
STUDY DESIGN: In November 2025, a national consensus conference convened 28 SPC experts and researchers. Through iterative discussion and consensus-building during the meeting and subsequent months, participants updated research priorities across the surgical continuum and health system context. Full methodology and participant attributes were described in Supplemental Materials https://links.lww.com/JACS/A821.
RESULTS: The updated agenda identified 11 research gaps across 3 priority areas: patient selection; interventions, care processes, and competencies; and outcome measurement. Priorities were mapped at 2 levels: surgical episodes, encompassing patient-, family-, and provider-level factors, and health systems, encompassing organizational and structural factors affecting SPC delivery. The agenda prioritizes identifying which patients benefit from SPC and when; broadening SPC beyond traditional populations; defining primary SPC competencies and the role of specialty consultation; improving communication of surgical intent, trade-offs, and preference-sensitive decisions; integrating and sustaining SPC across heterogeneous systems and care transitions; transforming clinical cultures; and developing patient-centered, context-specific surgical and systems-level outcomes. Emerging electronic health record, natural language processing, and large language model approaches may support scalable patient identification, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement, while requiring attention to bias and task-dependent performance.
CONCLUSIONS: SPC research should move beyond narrow proof-of-concept settings toward pragmatic, scalable approaches that define who should receive SPC, what should be delivered, and how success should be measured across diverse surgical environments.

makaleler.baslik: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Reconstruction Planning of Cheek Soft Tissue Defects: A Comparative Study Against Surgical Expert Consensus.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Yanak Yumuşak Doku Defektleri İçin Yapay Zeka Destekli Rekonstrüksiyon Planlaması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: ChatGPT-4o ile yanak defektleri rekonstrüksiyon yaklaşımları değerlendirilmiş ve ortalama 4,22/5 puan almıştır. Uzman değerlendiriciler arasında güçlü uyum (ICC=0,75, %95 CI 0,57-0,86, p<0,001) saptanmıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Reconstructive planning for cheek soft tissue defects requires expert assessment of defect size and location to preserve aesthetic harmony. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs), has emerged as a potential decision-support tool in plastic and reconstructive surgery. This study evaluates the accuracy and reliability of ChatGPT-4o in proposing reconstructive approaches for post-excisional cheek defects.
METHODS: A comparative observational image-based study was performed using 46 standardized oblique facial photographs of healthy volunteers, on which cheek soft tissue defects were manually delineated to simulate post-excisional tissue loss. Each annotated photograph was submitted to ChatGPT-4o alongside a standardized prompt incorporating patient-specific clinical data. Two experts independently rated AI-generated responses across five domains using a five-point Likert scale (1-5). Inter-rater agreement was assessed using Cohen's kappa and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).
RESULTS: ChatGPT-4o achieved high ratings across all domains: clinical accuracy 4.88/5, safety 4.59/5, aesthetic result 3.96/5, first reconstruction selection 4.05/5, and relevance of alternatives 3.65/5, with an average of 4.22/5. Strong inter-rater agreement was observed between evaluators (ICC = 0.75, 95% CI 0.57-0.86, p < 0.001), with high consistency for safety (κ = 0.82) and first reconstruction selection (κ = 0.76). However, ChatGPT-4o failed to generate illustrative depictions of the proposed reconstructive approaches.
CONCLUSION: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated strong concordance with expert evaluators and shows promise as a decision-support adjunct in cheek reconstructive planning. However, its inability to generate visual depictions of proposed flaps remains a notable limitation. Expert supervision remains indispensable, and prospective clinical validation is warranted before routine implementation.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE III: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

makaleler.baslik: Exploring perspectives and engagement in space surgery: a survey of SAGES members.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Uzay Cerrahisi Perspektifleri ve Katılımı: SAGES Üye Anketi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: SAGES üyeleriyle yapılan kesitsel ankete %6,1 oranında yanıt alındı; katılımcıların uzayda robotik teknolojilerin uygulanması ve uzay cerrahisi zorluklarına yönelik güçlü ilgi duyduğu belirlendi.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: SAGES' space surgery task force was created in 2023 in response to the potential increased need for surgical intervention in space as humanity seeks to establish larger and more permanent populations in space environments. This task force sought to assess the needs, limitations, and anticipated challenges of surgical care in space environments and to offer leadership opportunities by surveying the SAGES membership.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of the SAGES membership soliciting respondent's experience in aerospace medicine and related fields, as well as members' interests within space surgery and their opinions about the future surgical needs of space explorers. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize demographics, interests, and preferences, and narrative review and thematic analysis were used to analyze open-ended responses.
RESULTS: Survey response rate was 6.1%. Most respondents were attending minimally invasive or general surgeons. Experience was reported in telehealth, artificial intelligence, austere environment surgery, and military medicine. Greatest interest was expressed in the application of robotic technologies in space. Respondents wished to participate in technical skills workshops and to view presentations by astronauts on space medicine as part of the future activities of the task force at SAGES annual meetings. Themes identified as challenges to space surgery included microgravity, resource limitations, remote surgery, training, and specific medical concerns. Future areas of focus included technology and innovation, protocol/system design, adjustment to medical standards, and training programs.
CONCLUSION: This survey identified a strong interest among the SAGES membership in leading the conversation surrounding space surgery as humanity expands beyond low earth orbit. Numerous opportunities, challenges, and new directions were identified by respondents that will guide the future activities of the task force.

makaleler.baslik: From Accuracy to Adoption: A Clinical Readiness Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Orthopaedic Surgery (OSCAR).
makaleler.baslik_tr: Ortopedik Cerrahide Yapay Zeka İçin Klinik Hazırlık Çerçevesi (OSCAR)
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Yapay zeka araçlarının klinik değerlendirmesi için 6 aşamalı OSCAR kavramsal çerçevesi önerilmiştir. Bu çerçeve model geliştirme, validasyon ve izlenen klinik dağıtımı kapsamaktadır.
makaleler.ozet: Technical performance alone does not establish clinical readiness; strong accuracy or discrimination does not demonstrate that an artificial intelligence (AI) tool will generalize, improve clinical care, or remain safe after deployment. Existing AI frameworks provide important guidance for reporting, risk of bias, model evaluation, and clinical trials, but they do not provide a single longitudinal stage describing a technology's progression from development through monitored clinical deployment. We propose the Orthopaedic Surgery Clinical AI Readiness (OSCAR) scale as a 6-stage conceptual framework spanning model development, internal and external validation, early clinical evaluation, comparative clinical validation, and monitored deployment. Illustrative applications of OSCAR demonstrate how technically strong models may remain at stage 1, external validation advances a tool to stage 2, live workflow evaluation represents stage 3, and comparative clinical evidence is required for stage 4. OSCAR is intended to complement, not replace, established reporting and risk-of-bias standards. The framework remains unvalidated and requires stakeholder consensus, explicit decision criteria, inter-rater reliability testing, and prospective evaluation.

tez.baslik: Minimal invaziv adrenal cerrahide yapay zekâ destekli cerrahi kopilot: Anatomik yapılar, cerrahi aletler ve prosedür adımlarının entegre tanınması
tez.baslik_tr: Minimal İnvaziv Adrenal Cerrahide Yapay Zekâ Destekli Cerrahi Kopilot
tez.kisa_ozet: 20 hastaya ait 10747 cerrahi kare üzerinde geliştirilen ResNet-50 tabanlı model ile alet, aksiyon ve anatomik hedef tanımada sırasıyla %67,6, %86,2 ve %70,0 tek tahmin doğruluğuna ulaşılmıştır.
tez.ozet: Amaç Minimal invaziv adrenal cerrahilerde, anatomik yapıları, cerrahi aletleri ve prosedür adımlarını eş zamanlı tanıyabilen bir yapay zekâ destekli cerrahi asistan yazılımının geliştirilmesi ve klinik fizibilitesinin ortaya konması hedeflenmiştir. Bu sistemin, nadir uygulanan adrenal cerrahilerde, öğrenme sürecindeki cerrahları destekleyerek süreç güvenliğini artırma potansiyeli bulunmaktadır. Materyal ve Metot Ocak 2011 – Ocak 2025 arasında laparoskopik transabdominal adrenalektomi uygulanan, sağ ve soldan 10'ar olmak üzere toplam 20 hastanın video kayıtları retrospektif olarak incelendi ve çalışmaya dahil edildi. Videolardan elde edilen cerrahi kareler; cerrahi aletler, aksiyonlar, anatomik yapılar ve prosedür adımlarına göre işaretlenip sınıflandırılarak model eğitimine hazır hâle getirildi. Modelleme aşamasında ResNet-50 tabanlı, çok başlıklı bir çapraz-dikkat ağı yapısı kullanıldı. Model; alet, aksiyon, hedef anatomi ve prosedür adımı tahminleri için ayrı çıkış katmanlarına sahip olacak şekilde tasarlandı. Sağ ve sol adrenalektomiye özgü farkları dikkate alabilmek için yön bilgisi, özellik bazlı doğrusal modülasyon aracılığıyla ağa entegre edildi. Veri setindeki sınıf dengesizliği, frekanslara ters orantılı ağırlıklar kullanılan bir kayıp fonksiyonu ile giderildi. Modelin çoklu görev tanıma performansı, dengeli hasta ayrımıyla oluşturulan bağımsız bir test grubunda, en yüksek doğruluk ile ortalama kesinlik ve doğruluk değerleri üzerinden gerçekleştirildi. Bulgular Çalışmaya dahil edilen hastalardan elde edilen toplam 10.747 cerrahi kare, 9 alet kategorisi, 7 cerrahi aksiyon, 13 anatomik hedef ve 6 prosedür adımı olmak üzere 53.152 adet işaretleme ile etiketlendi. Model; cerrahi alet, aksiyon ve anatomik hedef tanımada sırasıyla %67,6, %86,2 ve %70,0 oranında tek tahmin doğruluğu; prosedür adımı tanımada ise %60,3 tek tahmin doğruluğuna ulaştı. İlk üç tahmin dikkate alındığında doğruluk oranları belirgin şekilde artarak aletlerde %93,8, aksiyonlarda %94,2, anatomik hedeflerde %90,9 ve prosedür adımı %95,3 seviyelerine yükseldi. Ortalama kesinlik sonuçları alet, aksiyon, hedef ve prosedür adımı için sırasıyla %64,2, %62,4, %46,8 ve %66,4 olarak hesaplandı. Sonuç Minimal invaziv adrenal cerrahiye yönelik geliştirilen yapay zekâ destekli model ile; cerrahi aletleri, anatomik yapıları ve prosedür adımlarını entegre biçimde ve yüksek performansla tanıyabilen bir sistemin fizibilitesi gösterildi. Bu sistemin intraoperatif karar destek mekanizması sağlayarak, cerrahi güvenliği artırma, komplikasyon riskini azaltma ve cerrahların eğitim sürecini nesnel geri bildirimle güçlendirme açısından geniş bir uygulama potansiyeli bulunmaktadır.

makaleler.baslik: Safety and Efficacy of Adjunctive Prophylactic Nitroimidazoles in Low-Risk Intraoral Tumor Resection: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
makaleler.baslik_tr: İntraoral Tümör Rezeksiyonunda Profilaktik Nitroimidazoller
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Düşük riskli intraoral tümör rezeksiyonu geçiren 160 erişkin hastanın dahil olduğu randomize kontrollü çalışmada, ek profilaktik nitroimidazol kullanımı 30 günlük SSI insidansını anlamlı düzeyde azaltmadı (ornidazol için %2,6, metronidazol için %5,1, tinidazol için %2,5 ve kontrol grubu için %7,5; P=0,781).
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infections (SSIs) in oral and maxillofacial surgery are predominantly polymicrobial, with anaerobes are involved in more than 70% of cases but are poorly detected by routine culture. Although guideline endorse nitroimidazoles as first-line prophylaxis, the considerable variation in resistance rates and safety profiles observed in practice has created a gap between evidence-based recommendations and clinical decision-making.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the safety and efficacy of metronidazole, tinidazole and ornidazole as adjunctive prophylactic agents for the prevention of SSI after low-risk intraoral tumor resection, and to provide evidence supporting the rational use of antibiotics.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, single-blind, single-center, exploratory trial, 160 adults undergoing low-risk intraoral tumor resection without flap reconstruction or implant placement were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive ornidazole, metronidazole, tinidazole, or cephalosporin-only control treatment. All participants received perioperative cefazolin prophylaxis. The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of SSI within 30 days postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included surgical incision healing, patient tolerance, and safety profile.
RESULTS: Of the 160 randomized patients, 3 were excluded after randomization because they met an exclusion criterion, leaving 157 patients in the full analysis set (ornidazole, n=38; metronidazole, n=39; tinidazole, n=40; control, n=40), of whom 146 (93.0%) completed the 30-day follow-up. The cumulative incidence of SSI, defined as an infection documented on postoperative day 3 or newly documented between day 3 and day 30, did not differ significantly among the four groups (P = 0.781): 2.6% (1/38) in the ornidazole group, 5.1% (2/39) in the metronidazole group, 2.5% (1/40) in the tinidazole group, and 7.5% (3/40) in the control group. Compared with the control group, the absolute risk differences in 30-day SSI were -4.9% (95% CI, -17.4 to 7.1) for ornidazole, -2.4% (95% CI, -15.3 to 10.4) for metronidazole, and -5.0% (95% CI, -17.5 to 6.5) for tinidazole; the corresponding conditional odds ratios were 0.33 (95% CI, 0.01-4.43), 0.67 (95% CI, 0.05-6.21) and 0.32 (95% CI, 0.01-4.20), respectively. One deep incisional infection occurred in the tinidazole group and one in the control group; no organ/space infection occurred in any group. No statistically significant differences were observed in surgical incision healing or patient tolerance among the groups. Adverse events were recorded in 9 patients (5.7%) within the first 3 days and in 45 of the 146 patients (30.8%) who completed follow-up by day 30, these were predominantly local wound-related reactions, with no significant difference among the groups (P = 0.525 for the day-3 comparison and P = 0.078 for the day-30 comparison) and mild gastrointestinal discomfort was reported in 8 patients (5.1%).
DISCUSSION: In this exploratory study, which was underpowered to detect small differences, adjunctive nitroimidazole prophylaxis did not significantly reduce the incidence of SSI. However, given the wide confidence intervals and limited statistical power, clinically meaningful benefit or harm cannot be excluded. These findings warrant confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials.
