makaleler.baslik: The Efficacy of Trocar-Assisted Percutaneous Abscess Drainage for Patients with Severe Acute Pancreatitis Complicated by Infected Pancreatic Necrosis.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Şiddetli Akut Pankreatitte Trokar Destekli Perkütan Apse Drenajı
makaleler.kisa_ozet: İnfekte pankreatik nekrozu olan 74 hastada yapılan retrospektif çalışmada, modifiye TA-PAD ve negatif basınçlı irrigasyon yöntemi geleneksel PCD'ye kıyasla daha düşük mortalite (%12,5'e karşı %34,6, p=0,024), daha kısa hastanede kalış süresi ve daha az re-intervansiyon (%20,8'e karşı %57,7, p<0,001) sağlamıştır.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUNDS: Traditional percutaneous catheter drainage (PCD) does not always achieve satisfactory therapeutic effects in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) complicated by infected pancreatic necrosis (IPN). We modified the conventional PCD therapy by employing Trocar-assisted percutaneous abscess drainage (TA-PAD) combined with double-lumen catheter negative-pressure irrigation and drainage for the treatment of patients with SAP with IPN and compared its efficacy with that of traditional PCD.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from patients with SAP complicated with IPN at Jinling Hospital between June 2018 and February 2024. Patients were divided by procedure into two treatment groups: the modified TA-PAD with negative-pressure irrigation group and the conventional PCD group, for comparative efficacy analysis.
RESULTS: Among the 74 patients, Comparison between the TA-PAD (n = 48) and PCD (n = 26) groups confirmed that TA-PAD was superior, yielding a lower mortality rate (12.5% vs. 34.6%, p = 0.024), shorter hospitalization (p = 0.006), reduced costs (p = 0.01), fewer re-interventions (20.8% vs. 57.7%, p < 0.001), and fewer catheters required (1 (1-2) vs. 2 (1-2.25), p = 0.029). Furthermore, the TA-PAD group demonstrated more significant improvements in infection markers, including body temperature, C-reactive protein, and white blood cell count.
CONCLUSION: The modified TA-PAD procedure combined with double-lumen catheter negative-pressure irrigation and drainage significantly outperformed conventional PCD in treating patients with SAP with IPN. The study demonstrates significant reductions in mortality, hospital stay, treatment costs, and procedural burden, alongside a superior resolution of infection markers within one week post-intervention.

makaleler.baslik: Accounting for urgency: Implications of risk adjustment for surgical site infection after emergency colon surgery at safety net hospitals.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Acil Kolon Cerrahisinde Cerrahi Alan İnfeksiyonu Risk Ayarlaması
makaleler.kisa_ozet: 2021 yılı verilerinin kullanıldığı çalışmada 360 hastane değerlendirilmiştir. Acil cerrahi göstergesinin risk modellerine eklenmesiyle, safety net hastanelerinin en yüksek SSI riski quintilindeki oranının azaldığı görülmüştür.
makaleler.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Colon operations performed for urgent indications or trauma are associated with a higher risk of surgical site infection. Prior models for surgical site infection surveillance did not account for this urgency, potentially yielding inadequate risk adjustment for surgical site infection at safety net hospitals that perform a disproportionate number of these emergency operations.
METHODS: We used data from the 2021 Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project State Inpatient and Emergency Department Databases from California and Florida. We evaluated index encounters during which colon surgery was performed, excluding hospitals performing <25 colon operations per year. We calculated risk- and reliability-adjusted surgical site infection rates, first adjusting for covariables modeled on the 2015 baseline National Healthcare Safety Network surgical site infection surveillance model, which did not account for trauma or emergency status: comorbidity index, diabetes, obesity, and endoscopic/laparoscopic approach; and subsequently adjusting for National Healthcare Safety Network-based covariables plus an indicator of emergency surgery. We then evaluated whether including this indicator affected the adjusted risk of surgical site infection among safety net hospitals and non-safety net hospitals.
RESULTS: We identified 360 hospitals that performed >25 colon operations in 2021, including 79 (22%) safety net hospitals. Safety net hospitals were more likely to be in the highest quintile of adjusted surgical site infection risk using the National Healthcare Safety Network-based covariates alone (P < .05) but not after adding the emergency surgery indicator to the model. The proportion of safety net hospitals in the highest quintile of adjusted surgical site infection risk decreased after accounting for emergency surgery.
CONCLUSION: Modifying risk adjustment models to include emergency status may reduce inadequate adjustment of surgical site infection risk after colon surgery, with important financial implications for safety net hospitals in the era of value-based incentives.

makaleler.baslik: Intra-operative oxygen concentration could affect postoperative morbidity-results of a randomised controlled feasibility trial (PULSE Ox).
makaleler.baslik_tr: İntraoperatif Oksijen Konsantrasyonunun Postoperatif Morbiditeye Etkisi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Kanser rezeksiyonu için major batın cerrahisi geçiren 28 erişkin hastanın randomize edildiği çalışmada, yüksek FIO2 düzeyleri daha düşük atelektazi oranları ile ilişkili bulundu (FIO2 0,30, 0,55 ve 0,80 için sırasıyla %75, %80 ve %30; p=0,045). Postoperatif enfektif morbidite ve kalış süresi gruplar arasında farklılık göstermedi.
makaleler.ozet: The World Health Organisation recommends that all anaesthetised patients receive FIO2 0.8 during surgery to reduce the risk of surgical site infections but did not consider the effect this might have on other clinical outcomes. A Cochrane systematic review concluded that insufficient evidence exists for routinely administering high oxygen concentrations intra-operatively to reduce surgical site infections, and that doing so might increase mortality. A feasibility trial was conducted looking at the feasibility of controlling intra-operative FIO2 and measuring systemic redox state. Here we explore further clinical outcomes from this study regarding postoperative complications and cognitive recovery. Twenty-eight adult patients undergoing major abdominal surgery for cancer resection were randomly allocated to receive either conservative (FIO2 = 0.3, n = 8), typical (FIO2 = 0.55, n = 10) or recommended (FIO2 = 0.8, n = 10) oxygen throughout anaesthesia. Rates of radiologically reported atelectasis, cognitive recovery and infective postoperative morbidity were all collected up to 7 days after surgery. Total intensive care unit length of stay was also recorded. Higher FIO2 levels were associated with lower rates of atelectasis - 6 (75%) versus 8 (80%) versus 3 (30%) for FIO2 = 0.30 versus 0.55 versus 0.80, respectively; p = 0.045. Postoperative cognitive recovery scores (0.7 (3.1) versus -0.1 (2.5) versus -1.8 (3.3), p = 0.277), Postoperative Morbidity Survey infection scores (5 (71%) versus 5 (56%) versus 3 (33%), p = 0.307) and intensive care unit length of stay (3 (2-4) versus 2.5 (2.00-3.75) versus 3 (2.00-5.25) days, p = 0.870) did not differ between groups. Changing the administered intra-operative oxygen concentration may alter postoperative clinical outcomes, and adequately powered clinical studies are urgently needed to investigate the impact of this.

makaleler.baslik: Evaluation of a mobile surgical air decontamination device in reducing airborne microbial load in the operating theatre of a tertiary care hospital.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Ameliyathanede Mobil Cerrahi Hava Dekontaminasyon Cihazının Değerlendirilmesi
makaleler.kisa_ozet: Yeni Delhi'deki bir hastanenin ameliyathanesinde gerçekleştirilen prospektif intervansiyonel çalışmada, mobil hava dekontaminasyon cihazı aktivasyonu sonrası ortalama toplam parçacık sayısı %40,42 azalmıştır. Ortalama havadan bulaşan mikrobiyal yük 34,47 CFU/m3'ten 15,20 CFU/m3'e anlamlı şekilde düşmüştür (P=0,0033).
makaleler.ozet:
INTRODUCTION: Microbiological air quality in the operating theatre (OT) plays a key role in preventing surgical site infections. Airborne particulate matter and microbes increase the risk of contamination during surgical procedures. Mobile air decontamination devices that integrate high-efficiency particulate air filtration with ultraviolet sterilization systems function as adjuncts to conventional ventilation systems to reduce airborne microbial load and improve microbiological air quality.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of a mobile air decontamination device in reducing airborne particulate matter and the microbial load in an OT at a tertiary care hospital.
METHODS: A prospective interventional study was conducted over a period of 15 days in an OT at a tertiary care hospital in New Delhi in July 2025. Air sampling for particle counts and colony forming units (CFU) was performed before and after device activation during routine OT functioning. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS.
RESULTS: The mean total particle count decreased from 6835.57 particles/m3 to 4071.97 particles/m3 after device activation, and showed an overall reduction of 40.42%. Significant reductions were seen in 0.3-μm (P = 0.0061) and 0.5-μm (P = 0.0088) particles. The mean airborne microbial load showed a significant reduction from 34.47 CFU/m3 to 15.20 CFU/m3 (P = 0.0033). The reduction in microbial count was consistent despite variations in OT activity.
CONCLUSION: The mobile air decontamination device improved air quality in the OT, and can be used as an adjunct to existing ventilation systems.

gundem.baslik: Acetic acid chromoendoscopy for detection of neoplastic Barrett's oesophagus: stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial (ACID-trial).
gundem.baslik_tr: Barrett Özofagus Sürveyansında Asetik Asit Kromoendoskopi
gundem.kisa_ozet: 2267 hastanın dahil olduğu çok merkezli step-wedge RCT'de, asetik asit kromoendoskopinin neoplazi saptama oranını artırmadığı gösterildi (%7,4'e karşı %7,1; OR 0,97; %95 CI 0,65-1,44).
gundem.ozet:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies.
DESIGN: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial.
SETTING: 18 Dutch community hospitals.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia.
INTERVENTIONS: Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies.
RESULTS: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24).
CONCLUSIONS: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl; NL-OMON25059 (prospective registration; 4 Dec 2019).

gundem.baslik: Cold versus hot snare endoscopic mucosal resection for 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps: a multicenter randomized trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: 10-19 mm Kolorektal Poliplerde Soğuk ve Sıcak Snare EMR
gundem.kisa_ozet: 233 polibin alındığı çok merkezli RCT'de, soğuk snare EMR tam histolojik rezeksiyon açısından sıcak snare EMR'ye benzer bulundu (%90,4'e karşı %93,2; fark -%2,7; %95 CI -%9,8 - %4,3). Soğuk grupta işlem içi kanama daha sık görüldü (%19,1'e karşı %3,4).
gundem.ozet:
BACKGROUND: Evidence for cold snare endoscopic mucosal resection (CS-EMR) in 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps is scarce. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) to compare CS-EMR against hot snare EMR (HS-EMR) in this setting.
METHODS: We enrolled patients with 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps from 15 centers. Eligible polyps were individually randomized (1:1) to CS-EMR or HS-EMR. The primary outcome was histologic complete resection, analyzed in modified intention-to-treat (mITT) and per-protocol (PP) populations (noninferiority margin -10%). Secondary outcomes included en bloc resection, intraprocedural and delayed adverse events, and resection time.
RESULTS: 216 patients with 233 eligible polyps were included (CS-EMR 116; HS-EMR 117). In the mITT analysis, complete resection was 90.4% in the CS-EMR group and 93.2% in the HS-EMR group (difference -2.7%, 95%CI -9.8 to 4.3), showing noninferiority of CS-EMR vs. HS-EMR. PP results were consistent (CS-EMR 93.3%; HS-EMR 93.2%; difference 0.2%, 95%CI -6.7 to 7.1). CS-EMR was noninferior for 10-14-mm polyps (94.3% vs. 94.0%; 95%CI -6.8 to 7.2) but not for 15-19-mm polyps (78.6% vs. 90.9%; 95%CI -30.4 to 5.8), although interaction was not significant. En bloc resection rates and resection time were similar between groups. Intraprocedural bleeding was more frequent with CS-EMR (19.1% vs. 3.4%), whereas delayed bleeding was rare (0.0% vs. 0.9%), and no perforation occurred in either group.
CONCLUSION: CS-EMR was noninferior to HS-EMR for histologic complete resection of 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps, but its applicability to 15-19-mm lesions remains uncertain.

gundem.baslik: Lymph node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic cancer: the randomized phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: Pankreas Kanserinde mKRAS Hedefli Aşı: Faz 2 AMPLIFY-7P Çalışması
gundem.kisa_ozet: Evre I-III KRAS mutasyonlu PDAC hastalarında camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) aşısının değerlendirildiği 144 hastalık faz 2 RCT'de, birincil DFS sonlanım noktasına ulaşılamadı (ortanca 23,8'e karşı 21,2 ay; HR 0,85, P=0,5329). Ancak önceden belirlenmiş analizlerde 6. ayda %14,0'lık sayısal bir DFS avantajı ve multivaryant analizlerde camupepimut lehine iyileşme görüldü (düzenlenmiş HR 0,47, P=0,0086). Güvenlik profili gözlem grubuyla benzerdi.
gundem.ozet: Camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) drives mutated KRAS (mKRAS)-specific T cell responses that correlated with disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with mKRAS pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial. In the phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial, patients with stage I-III KRAS-mutated PDAC without recurrence within 6 months of standard therapy were randomized 2:1 to camupepimut (n = 96) or standard-of-care/observation (n = 48). Stratification balanced nodal status. The primary DFS endpoint was not met (median 23.8 versus 21.2 months; HR 0.85, P = 0.5329). However, prespecified and exploratory analyses were informative. A numerical DFS advantage at 6 months of 14.0% (75.7% versus 61.7%; HR 0.55, P = 0.0557) corresponded to camupepimut dosing. Post hoc multivariate Cox regression analysis of DFS indicated an improved outcome for camupepimut (adjusted HR 0.47, P = 0.0086), a worse outcome for stage III disease (adjusted HR 2.29, P = 0.0127), an elevated baseline CA19-9 (adjusted HR 3.16, P < 0.0001) and baseline circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) positivity (adjusted HR 5.99, P < 0.0001). Prespecified subgroup analyses addressing prognostic and predictive factors suggested DFS benefit for camupepimut (ctDNA negative: HR 0.51, P = 0.0280; no prior radiation: HR 0.59, P = 0.0221). Exploratory analysis demonstrated that ex vivo mKRAS-specific T cell responses were robust (98.9%, 89/90) and associated with antigen spreading (86.7%, 13/15). In camupepimut-treated patients, mKRAS-specific T cell response >9.17-fold over baseline (82.2%, 74/90) correlated with improved DFS (HR 0.22, P < 0.0001), with the median DFS not reached versus 6.08 months for above and below 9.17-fold, respectively. Camupepimut safety was similar to observation, with grade ≥3 adverse events in 10.4% (10/96) versus 14.6% (7/48), and few serious AEs (6.3%, 6/96 versus 8.3%, 4/48; reflecting progression/surgical complication). These efficacy and immunogenicity signals will inform a refined strategy for a confirmatory phase 3 trial. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05726864 .

gundem.baslik: Hypofractionated Versus Conventionally Fractionated Postmastectomy Radiotherapy With Internal Mammary Node Irradiation for High-Risk Breast Cancer (HypoMast-IMNI): A Randomized Phase III Trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: Meme Kanseri ve Radyoterapi: HypoMast-IMNI Faz III Çalışması
gundem.kisa_ozet: Yüksek riskli operabl meme kanserinde 1.494 hastayla yapılan faz III RCT'de, 16 fraksiyonda hipofraksiyone radyoterapi (HypoRT), locoregional kontrol açısından konvansiyonel radyoterapiye (ConvRT) noninferior bulundu (5 yıllık LRR %1,7'ye karşı %2,2; HR 0,69; p=0,017). HypoRT'de grade 3 akut cilt toksisitesi anlamlı derecede düşüktü (%1,7'ye karşı %12,2; p<0,001).
gundem.ozet:
PURPOSE: When coverage of internal mammary nodes (IMN) is required, the efficacy and safety of hypofractionated regimens within postmastectomy radiotherapy (PMRT) remain to be established. This study evaluated hypofractionated radiotherapy (HypoRT) in patients with high-risk, operable breast cancer undergoing PMRT with IMN irradiation (IMNI).
METHODS: In this phase III noninferiority trial, eligible patients with high-risk disease after mastectomy (including pT1-4N2-3, pT3-4N1, or pT1-2N1 disease with additional high-risk factors) were randomly assigned (1:1) to HypoRT (42.56 Gy in 16 fractions) or conventionally fractionated radiotherapy (ConvRT; 50 Gy in 25 fractions), both targeting the chest wall and regional lymph nodes, including the IMN. The primary end point was locoregional recurrence (LRR). Secondary end points were distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), breast cancer recurrence-free survival (BCRFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and treatment-related toxicity. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov (identifier: NCT03856372).
RESULTS: Between September 2018 and July 2022, 1,494 patients were randomly assigned. After a median follow-up of 58.1 months in the modified intention-to-treat population (n = 1,429), the 5-year cumulative incidence of LRR was 1.7% (95% CI, 0.9 to 2.9) with HypoRT and 2.2% (95% CI, 1.3 to 3.5) with ConvRT (hazard ratio, 0.69 [95% CI, 0.32 to 1.51]), meeting the noninferiority criterion (P = .017). No significant differences were observed in 5-year DMFS, BCRFS, DFS, or OS. Grade 3 acute skin toxicity was significantly lower with HypoRT (1.7% v 12.2%, P < .001). The incidence of grade ≥2 radiation pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis was low and comparable between arms, with no ischemic cardiac events recorded.
CONCLUSION: For patients with high-risk, operable breast cancer requiring PMRT with IMNI, the 16-fraction HypoRT regimen is noninferior to ConvRT for locoregional control, offers a superior acute toxicity profile, and demonstrates excellent cardiopulmonary safety.

gundem.baslik: Subtotal Colectomy vs Total Colectomy for Slow-Transit Constipation: 1-Year Outcomes of the STOPS Randomized Clinical Trial.
gundem.baslik_tr: Yavaş Geçişli Kabızlıkta Subtotal ve Total Kolektomi Karşılaştırması
gundem.kisa_ozet: Yavaş geçişli kabızlığı olan 252 hastanın dahil olduğu multicenter RCT'de, 12. ayda Wexner Constipation Score yönünden SC-CRA, TC-IRA'ya noninferior bulundu (ortalama skorlar sırasıyla 7,01 ve 6,84; p=0,02). 3. ayda erken evre inkontinans SC-CRA grubunda daha düşüktü (%8,7'ye karşı %21,4; p=0,01), ancak 1 yıllık hasta memnuniyeti TC-IRA grubunda daha yüksekti (%97,5'e karşı %95,8; p=0,03).
gundem.ozet:
IMPORTANCE: For patients with slow-transit constipation (STC), total colectomy with ileorectal anastomosis (TC-IRA) remains the standard surgical treatment but is frequently complicated by diarrhea, fecal incontinence, and bowel obstruction. Subtotal colectomy with cecorectal anastomosis (SC-CRA) has emerged as a promising alternative; however, recurrence of constipation remains a critical concern. High-quality evidence comparing these 2 procedures is lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the 1-year Wexner Constipation Score of patients with STC who underwent SC-CRA vs TC-IRA.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, open-label, noninferiority randomized clinical trial was conducted at 12 tertiary hospitals across 8 provinces in China from April 2022 to April 2025, with 12-month follow-up (final follow-up April 2026). Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older with Rome IV-defined functional constipation, fewer than 1 spontaneous bowel movement per week, and long-term laxative dependence, defined as the regular use of osmotic or stimulant laxatives, or prokinetic agents, at least 3 times weekly for 6 months or longer before enrollment. Of 272 adults assessed, 252 were randomized. These data were analyzed from March 2025 to March 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo either SC-CRA or TC-IRA.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the Wexner Constipation Score (WCS) at 12 months, with a prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.32 points. Secondary outcomes included fecal incontinence, morbidity, quality of life, and patient-reported satisfaction.
RESULTS: A total of 252 participants (mean age, 49.5 years; 221 female [87.7%] and 31 male [12.3%]) were randomized to undergo SC-CRA (n = 126) or TC-IRA (n = 126). At 12 months, adjusted mean (SD) WCS was 7.01 (3.31) in the SC-CRA group and 6.84 (3.68) in the TC-IRA group (adjusted mean difference, 0.17; 95% CI, -0.93 to 1.27), which fell within the prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.32 (P = .02 for noninferiority). Early postoperative incontinence at 3 months was less frequent in the SC-CRA group than in the TC-IRA group (8.7% vs 21.4%; risk difference, -12.7%; 95% CI, -21.4% to -4.0%; P = .01). Perioperative morbidity did not differ significantly between groups (10.3% vs 12.7%; risk difference, -2.4%; 95% CI, -10.3% to 5.5%; P = .41), and quality-of-life scores at 12 months were comparable. However, patient-reported satisfaction at 12 months favored the TC-IRA group (97.5% vs 95.8%; P = .03).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial among patients with refractory STC, SC-CRA was noninferior to TC-IRA with respect to the WCS at 12 months, but patient-reported satisfaction at 1 year was higher in the TC-IRA group. Longer-term follow-up is needed.
